title: Cadê as chaves?
text:
Ontem, Marcos chegou do trabalho às sete da noite, cansado. Na porta do apartamento, procurou as chaves na mochila, mas não encontrou. Ligou para a esposa, Lúcia, mas ela não atendeu.

Marcos desceu e falou com o porteiro do prédio, o Antônio. Os dois procuraram as chaves no carro e na garagem. Nada!

Às oito e meia, Lúcia chegou e abriu a porta. As chaves estavam na mesa da sala. Marcos riu e disse: “Amanhã, vou olhar a mesa antes de sair!”
translation:
Yesterday Marcos got home from work at seven in the evening, tired. At the apartment door, he looked for his keys in his backpack, but he didn't find them. He called his wife, Lúcia, but she didn't answer.

Marcos went downstairs and talked to the building's doorman, Antônio. The two of them looked for the keys in the car and in the garage. Nothing!

At half past eight, Lúcia arrived and opened the door. The keys were on the living-room table. Marcos laughed and said, “Tomorrow I'm going to look at the table before I leave!”

questions.q: What is the story about?
questions.explain: At his door Marcos 'procurou as chaves ... mas não encontrou' (looked for his keys but didn't find them).

questions.q: Where were the keys in the end?
questions.explain: When Lúcia opens the door, 'As chaves estavam na mesa da sala' (on the living-room table).

questions.q: Who is Antônio?
questions.explain: Marcos goes downstairs and talks to 'o porteiro do prédio, o Antônio': a 'porteiro' looks after the entrance of a building.

topic: ordering the dish of the day
title: O prato do dia
text:
— Boa tarde! Aqui está o cardápio.
— Obrigado. Qual é o prato do dia?
— Hoje é quarta-feira, então tem feijoada. Vem com arroz, couve, farofa e laranja.
— Que bom! Eu comi a feijoada de vocês no mês passado, e estava ótima. O prato é grande?
— É, sim. Serve duas pessoas. Mas também tem meia porção.
— Então, meia porção, por favor.
— E para beber?
— Uma limonada sem gelo.
— Mais alguma coisa?
— Não, obrigado.
— Certo. A feijoada fica pronta em dez minutos.
translation:
— Good afternoon! Here's the menu.
— Thank you. What's the dish of the day?
— Today is Wednesday, so there's feijoada. It comes with rice, collard greens, farofa and orange.
— Great! I had your feijoada last month, and it was excellent. Is the dish big?
— Yes, it is. It serves two people. But there's also a half portion.
— A half portion, then, please.
— And to drink?
— A lemonade with no ice.
— Anything else?
— No, thank you.
— Right. The feijoada will be ready in ten minutes.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.explain: The waiter brings 'o cardápio' (the menu), and the customer asks about 'o prato do dia', the feijoada, and orders it with a drink.

questions.q: What does the customer want to drink?
questions.explain: He asks for 'Uma limonada sem gelo' ('sem' means without).

questions.q: The waiter says the dish 'Serve duas pessoas.' What does this mean?
options: Two waiters bring it to you
It takes two hours to cook
It is enough for two people
It costs as much as two drinks
questions.explain: Asked if the dish is big, the waiter says 'Serve duas pessoas' and offers 'meia porção' (a half portion), so the full dish feeds two.

topic: asking a colleague to swap shifts
title: Um favor
text:
Larissa: Oi, Pedro! Posso te pedir um favor?
Pedro: Claro! Pode falar.
Larissa: Você pode trabalhar no meu lugar no sábado de manhã? A formatura do meu irmão é às dez, e depois tem um almoço com a família.
Pedro: No sábado eu tenho aula de inglês, mas só às quatro da tarde. Então, posso, sim!
Larissa: Que ótimo! Em troca, eu trabalho no seu lugar no domingo que vem.
Pedro: Combinado! Avisa a gerente, tá?
Larissa: Vou avisar agora mesmo. Valeu!
translation:
Larissa: Hi, Pedro! Can I ask you a favor?
Pedro: Sure! Go ahead.
Larissa: Can you work in my place on Saturday morning? My brother's graduation is at ten, and afterwards there's a lunch with the family.
Pedro: On Saturday I have an English class, but only at four in the afternoon. So yes, I can!
Larissa: Great! In return, I'll work in your place next Sunday.
Pedro: Deal! Tell the manager, OK?
Larissa: I'll tell her right now. Thanks!

questions.q: Why does Larissa write to Pedro?
options: To invite him to a party
To ask about his English class
To say she is leaving her job
To ask him to work for her
questions.explain: Larissa asks 'Você pode trabalhar no meu lugar...?' (can you work in my place?).

questions.q: When is Pedro's English class?
questions.explain: Pedro writes 'No sábado eu tenho aula de inglês, mas só às quatro da tarde'.

questions.q: Pedro writes 'Avisa a gerente, tá?' Who is 'a gerente'?
questions.explain: Larissa and Pedro are changing their work days, so they must tell 'a gerente', the woman in charge at their job.

title: Estou chegando!
text:
Júlia: Oi, Bruna! Já cheguei ao bar. Peguei uma mesa perto da janela. Cadê você?
Bruna: Desculpa, Júlia! Ainda estou no caminho. O meu ônibus quebrou no meio da avenida, e agora estou esperando outro.
Júlia: Ah, que chato! Você vai demorar muito?
Bruna: Uns vinte minutos, acho. Pode pedir alguma coisa para beber.
Júlia: Tudo bem. Vou pedir um suco e esperar você para comer.
Bruna: Obrigada! Pede também uma porção de pastel para a gente?
Júlia: Pode deixar!
translation:
Júlia: Hi, Bruna! I've got to the bar. I got a table near the window. Where are you?
Bruna: Sorry, Júlia! I'm still on my way. My bus broke down in the middle of the avenue, and now I'm waiting for another one.
Júlia: Oh, what a pain! Will you be long?
Bruna: About twenty minutes, I think. You can order something to drink.
Júlia: OK. I'll order a juice and wait for you before I eat.
Bruna: Thanks! Can you also order a portion of pastéis for us?
Júlia: Leave it to me!

questions.q: What is the chat mainly about?
options: Bruna is late to meet Júlia
Bruna wants to cancel their plans
questions.explain: Júlia is already at the bar and asks 'Cadê você?', and Bruna answers 'Ainda estou no caminho' (I'm still on my way).

questions.q: What happened to Bruna's bus?
questions.explain: Bruna writes 'O meu ônibus quebrou no meio da avenida' (my bus broke down in the middle of the avenue).

questions.q: Júlia answers 'Pode deixar!' What does she mean?
questions.explain: Bruna asks Júlia to order 'uma porção de pastel', and 'Pode deixar!' is a friendly yes: Júlia will do it.

title: Bicicleta à venda
text:
VENDO BICICLETA
Vendo uma bicicleta azul, de adulto, em ótimo estado. Comprei no ano passado, mas usei pouco, porque mudei de emprego e agora vou de carro para o trabalho.
A bicicleta tem luzes na frente e atrás e uma cesta grande. Também vendo o capacete, que nunca usei.

Preço: R$ 700,00 (com o capacete, R$ 780,00).
Você pode ver e testar a bicicleta no sábado ou no domingo, na garagem do prédio.

Interessados, falem com o Rodrigo, do apartamento 501.
translation:
BIKE FOR SALE
I'm selling a blue adult's bike in excellent condition. I bought it last year, but I've hardly used it, because I changed jobs and now I drive to work.
The bike has lights at the front and back and a big basket. I'm also selling the helmet, which I've never used.

Price: R$ 700.00 (with the helmet, R$ 780.00).
You can see and try out the bike on Saturday or Sunday, in the building's garage.

If you're interested, talk to Rodrigo in apartment 501.

questions.q: What is this advert for?
questions.explain: The heading 'VENDO BICICLETA' means 'I'm selling a bike', and Rodrigo bought it 'no ano passado' (last year).

questions.q: Why doesn't Rodrigo use the bike much?
options: It is too small for him
He has a new, faster bike
questions.explain: Rodrigo writes 'usei pouco, porque mudei de emprego e agora vou de carro para o trabalho' (now I go to work by car).

questions.q: How much extra does the helmet cost?
questions.explain: The bike is 'R$ 700,00', and 'com o capacete' (with the helmet) it is 'R$ 780,00', so the helmet adds R$ 80,00.

topic: adopting a dog at a fair
title: Um novo amigo
text:
No mês passado, a família Oliveira foi a uma feira de adoção de animais, num parque de Curitiba. Lá, tinha muitos cães e gatos sem casa.

As crianças, Davi e Laura, queriam um cachorro pequeno. Mas um cachorro grande e marrom olhou para eles e balançou o rabo. Foi amor à primeira vista! Eles levaram o cachorro para casa, e ele ganhou um nome: Biscoito.

Hoje, Biscoito dorme na sala e passeia com as crianças todas as tardes.
translation:
Last month, the Oliveira family went to a pet adoption fair in a park in Curitiba. There were lots of dogs and cats there without a home.

The children, Davi and Laura, wanted a small dog. But a big brown dog looked at them and wagged its tail. It was love at first sight! They took the dog home, and he got a name: Biscoito.

Today Biscoito sleeps in the living room and goes for a walk with the children every afternoon.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: A family adopting a small dog
Two children finding a lost dog
A family adopting a big dog
A family buying a dog at a shop
questions.explain: At 'uma feira de adoção' the family took home 'um cachorro grande e marrom', though the children 'queriam um cachorro pequeno'.

questions.q: When does Biscoito go for walks?
questions.explain: The text says Biscoito 'passeia com as crianças todas as tardes' (every afternoon).

questions.q: The brown dog 'balançou o rabo'. What did he do?
questions.explain: He looked at the children and 'balançou o rabo': a 'rabo' is a tail, and 'balançar' is to move it from side to side.

title: Sol demais
text:
— Boa tarde! Posso ajudar?
— Boa tarde. Ontem eu fui à praia e esqueci o protetor solar. Agora as minhas costas estão vermelhas e doem muito.
— Nossa, que queimadura! Use este creme três vezes por dia, depois do banho.
— Quanto custa?
— Trinta reais. E beba bastante água, tá?
— Certo. E amanhã? Posso ir à praia de novo?
— Melhor não. Fique em casa ou na sombra por uns três dias.
— Que pena! Mas tudo bem. Vou levar o creme e um protetor solar também.
translation:
— Good afternoon! Can I help you?
— Good afternoon. Yesterday I went to the beach and forgot my sunscreen. Now my back is red and it hurts a lot.
— Oh dear, what a burn! Use this cream three times a day, after your shower.
— How much is it?
— Thirty reais. And drink plenty of water, OK?
— Right. And tomorrow? Can I go to the beach again?
— Better not. Stay at home or in the shade for about three days.
— What a shame! But that's OK. I'll take the cream and some sunscreen too.

questions.q: Where does this conversation happen?
questions.explain: The customer asks 'Quanto custa?' and says 'Vou levar o creme e um protetor solar também' (I'll take...), so it is a shop that sells medicine.

questions.q: How often must the cream be used?
questions.explain: The pharmacist says 'Use este creme três vezes por dia, depois do banho'.

questions.q: What will the sunburned person probably do tomorrow?
options: Go back to the beach early
Spend the day at a pool
Stay at home or in the shade
questions.explain: The pharmacist says 'Melhor não. Fique em casa ou na sombra...', and the customer accepts: 'Que pena! Mas tudo bem.'

title: Aviso aos moradores
text:
AVISO AOS MORADORES
Na próxima terça-feira, dia 12, vamos limpar a caixa d'água do prédio. Por isso, não vai ter água nos apartamentos das 8h às 16h.

Por favor, guardem água em baldes e garrafas na segunda à noite. E não usem a máquina de lavar roupa na terça.
Nós limpamos a caixa d'água duas vezes por ano, porque água limpa é importante para a saúde de todos.

Em caso de dúvida, falem com o porteiro.
Agradecemos a compreensão!
A Administração
translation:
NOTICE TO RESIDENTS
Next Tuesday, the 12th, we are going to clean the building's water tank. Because of this, there will be no water in the apartments from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Please store water in buckets and bottles on Monday evening. And don't use the washing machine on Tuesday.
We clean the water tank twice a year, because clean water is important for everyone's health.

If you have any questions, talk to the doorman.
Thank you for your understanding!
The Management

questions.q: What is the notice about?
options: A new water tank for the building
A problem with dirty tap water
A higher water bill this month
Water will be off for some hours
questions.explain: It says 'não vai ter água nos apartamentos das 8h às 16h' (there will be no water from 8 to 4) on Tuesday, while the tank is cleaned.

questions.q: How often is the water tank cleaned?
questions.explain: The notice says 'Nós limpamos a caixa d'água duas vezes por ano'.

questions.q: 'Em caso de dúvida, falem com o porteiro.' When should residents talk to the doorman?
options: When they go out to work
questions.explain: 'Dúvida' means a doubt or question: anyone who is not sure about something should 'falem com o porteiro'.

title: Uma manhã fria
text:
Assunto: Problema no chuveiro
Bom dia, Sr. Paulo!
Aqui é a Renata, que aluga o seu apartamento na Rua Bahia. Ontem à noite, o chuveiro elétrico parou de funcionar. Acho que queimou. Hoje de manhã, tomei banho frio, e está fazendo muito frio aqui em Porto Alegre!

O senhor pode mandar um eletricista esta semana? Trabalho de segunda a sexta, mas estou em casa depois das 18h e no sábado de manhã.

Obrigada!
Renata Souza
translation:
Subject: Problem with the shower
Good morning, Mr. Paulo!
This is Renata, who rents your apartment on Rua Bahia. Last night the electric shower stopped working. I think it burned out. This morning I had a cold shower, and it's very cold here in Porto Alegre!

Could you send an electrician this week? I work Monday to Friday, but I'm at home after 6 p.m. and on Saturday morning.

Thank you!
Renata Souza

questions.q: Why does Renata write to Mr. Paulo?
questions.explain: The subject is 'Problema no chuveiro', and she writes that the electric shower 'parou de funcionar' (stopped working).

questions.q: When did the problem start?
questions.explain: Renata writes 'Ontem à noite, o chuveiro elétrico parou de funcionar'; the cold shower came later, this morning.

questions.q: Who is Mr. Paulo?
questions.explain: Renata 'aluga o seu apartamento' (rents his apartment), so the apartment is his, and she asks him to send 'um eletricista'.

topic: a small haircut at the salon
title: No salão
text:
— Boa tarde! Você tem horário agora?
— Tenho, sim. O que você vai fazer hoje?
— Quero cortar o cabelo, mas só um pouco. Da última vez, em outro salão, cortaram demais, e eu fiquei muito triste.
— Entendi. Então, vou cortar só as pontas, uns dois dedos. Pode ser?
— Pode. E você também faz escova?
— Faço, sim. O corte com escova fica oitenta reais.
— Tudo bem. Ah, e quanto tempo demora?
— Uns quarenta minutos. Pode sentar aqui, por favor.
translation:
— Good afternoon! Do you have a free slot now?
— Yes, I do. What are you having done today?
— I want a haircut, but just a little. Last time, at another salon, they cut too much, and I was really upset.
— I see. So I'll just cut the ends, about two fingers. Is that OK?
— Yes. And do you do blow-drys too?
— Yes, I do. The cut with a blow-dry is eighty reais.
— All right. Oh, and how long does it take?
— About forty minutes. Please sit here.

questions.q: What is the customer worried about?
options: That it will cost too much
That they will cut too much
That it will take too long
That there is no time today
questions.explain: The customer says that last time, at another salon, 'cortaram demais' (they cut too much) and 'eu fiquei muito triste' (I was really upset).

questions.q: How much do the cut and blow-dry cost?
questions.explain: The hairdresser says 'O corte com escova fica oitenta reais'.

questions.q: The hairdresser will cut 'as pontas'. Which part of the hair is that?
questions.explain: 'Pontas' are the ends: the customer wants 'só um pouco', so the hairdresser offers 'só as pontas, uns dois dedos' (just the ends, about two fingers).

topic: summer rain and an old friend
title: Chuva de verão
text:
Numa sexta-feira de janeiro, em São Paulo, Bianca saiu do trabalho às seis. De manhã, o dia estava lindo, então ela não levou guarda-chuva. Mas, na rua, começou uma chuva forte.

Bianca correu para uma cafeteria e pediu um chocolate quente. De repente, alguém chamou o nome dela. Era a Tatiane, uma amiga da escola! Fazia quinze anos que elas não se viam.

As duas conversaram por duas horas. Quando a chuva parou, Bianca pensou: “Ainda bem que eu não trouxe guarda-chuva!”
translation:
One Friday in January, in São Paulo, Bianca left work at six. In the morning the day was beautiful, so she didn't take an umbrella. But out in the street, heavy rain started.

Bianca ran into a café and ordered a hot chocolate. Suddenly someone called her name. It was Tatiane, a friend from school! They hadn't seen each other for fifteen years.

The two of them talked for two hours. When the rain stopped, Bianca thought, “Good thing I didn't bring an umbrella!”

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: Bianca is late for a family dinner
Bianca can't go to work in the rain
Bianca's day at the park is ruined
Bianca meets an old friend by chance
questions.explain: In the café, 'De repente, alguém chamou o nome dela': it was Tatiane, 'uma amiga da escola', and they 'conversaram por duas horas'.

questions.q: What did Bianca order at the café?
questions.explain: The text says 'Bianca correu para uma cafeteria e pediu um chocolate quente'.

questions.q: At the end Bianca thinks 'Ainda bem que eu não trouxe guarda-chuva!' What does she mean?
options: She is glad she had no umbrella
She is sorry she had no umbrella
She wants to buy a new umbrella
She left her umbrella at work
questions.explain: 'Ainda bem que' means 'it's a good thing that': with no umbrella she ran into the café, where she met her friend.

title: Falta do Lucas
text:
Assunto: Falta do Lucas
Prezada professora Sandra,
Sou a mãe do Lucas Ferreira, do 3º ano B. Infelizmente, o Lucas não vai poder ir à escola esta semana. Ontem à noite, ele teve febre alta, e hoje de manhã nós fomos ao médico. É uma gripe forte, e ele precisa ficar em casa.

O Lucas está triste, porque ia apresentar o trabalho de Ciências na quinta-feira. Ele pode apresentar na semana que vem?
Envio o atestado médico em anexo.

Obrigada,
Patrícia Ferreira
translation:
Subject: Lucas's absence
Dear Ms. Sandra,
I'm the mother of Lucas Ferreira, from class 3B. Unfortunately, Lucas won't be able to go to school this week. Last night he had a high fever, and this morning we went to the doctor. It's a bad flu, and he needs to stay at home.

Lucas is sad because he was going to present his science project on Thursday. Can he present it next week?
I'm attaching the doctor's note.

Thank you,
Patrícia Ferreira

questions.q: Why does Patrícia write to the teacher?
options: Lucas hurt his leg at football
Lucas sees a doctor on Thursday
Lucas is sick and must stay home
Lucas is going on a family trip
questions.explain: She writes 'ele teve febre alta' and 'É uma gripe forte, e ele precisa ficar em casa'.

questions.q: What was Lucas going to do on Thursday?
questions.explain: Patrícia writes that Lucas 'ia apresentar o trabalho de Ciências na quinta-feira' (was going to present his science project).

questions.q: Patrícia sends 'o atestado médico' with the email. What is it?
questions.explain: They went 'ao médico' (to the doctor), and the 'atestado médico' is the doctor's note that explains why Lucas is missing school.

title: A vovó e o celular
text:
Dona Lurdes tem setenta e oito anos e mora em Recife. Os netos dela moram em São Paulo. Eles sempre mandavam mensagens no celular, mas as letras eram pequenas demais, e ela quase nunca respondia.

Em julho, a neta Marina veio visitar e ensinou a avó a mandar áudios. É só apertar um botão e falar!

Agora, Dona Lurdes manda áudios todos os dias. Eles duram cinco ou seis minutos! Os netos acham engraçado, mas adoram ouvir a voz da avó.
translation:
Dona Lurdes is seventy-eight and lives in Recife. Her grandchildren live in São Paulo. They always used to send her messages on her phone, but the letters were too small, and she almost never answered.

In July, her granddaughter Marina came to visit and taught her grandmother to send voice messages. You just press a button and talk!

Now Dona Lurdes sends voice messages every day. They last five or six minutes! Her grandchildren find it funny, but they love hearing their grandmother's voice.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: Dona Lurdes learns to send voice messages
Dona Lurdes buys her very first cell phone
Dona Lurdes teaches Marina to cook
questions.explain: Marina 'ensinou a avó a mandar áudios', and now Dona Lurdes 'manda áudios todos os dias'.

questions.q: Which city do Dona Lurdes's grandchildren live in?
questions.explain: The text says 'Os netos dela moram em São Paulo'; Dona Lurdes lives in Recife.

questions.q: 'Os netos acham engraçado.' What do the grandchildren think?
questions.explain: 'Engraçado' means funny: the five- or six-minute voice messages amuse them, 'mas adoram ouvir a voz da avó' (but they love hearing her voice).

title: A casa é sua!
text:
Fernanda: Oi, Diego! Deixei a chave do apartamento com o porteiro para você. A senha da internet está na porta da geladeira.
Fernanda: Só um pedido: regue as plantas da varanda dia sim, dia não. Elas precisam de pouca água, só meio copo cada uma.
Diego: Tranquilo! E o lixo?
Fernanda: Deixe o lixo na lixeira do corredor, ao lado do elevador. Ah, e não abra a janela da sala à noite, porque entra muito mosquito!
Diego: Beleza. Boa viagem!
translation:
Fernanda: Hi, Diego! I left the key to the apartment with the doorman for you. The internet password is on the fridge door.
Fernanda: Just one request: water the plants on the balcony every other day. They need very little water, only half a glass each.
Diego: No problem! What about the trash?
Fernanda: Leave the trash in the bin in the hallway, next to the elevator. Oh, and don't open the living-room window at night, because lots of mosquitoes come in!
Diego: Cool. Have a good trip!

questions.q: Why does Fernanda write to Diego?
options: To invite him to live with her
To ask him to look after her two cats
To explain how to look after her home
To ask him to find her a new home
questions.explain: She left 'a chave do apartamento' for him and explains what to do there, and Diego answers 'Boa viagem!' (have a good trip).

questions.q: Where should Diego leave the trash?
options: In the bin in the hallway
questions.explain: Fernanda writes 'Deixe o lixo na lixeira do corredor, ao lado do elevador'.

questions.q: Fernanda asks Diego to water the plants 'dia sim, dia não'. How often is that?
questions.explain: 'Dia sim, dia não' is 'one day yes, one day no': the plants get water every other day.

title: Ligação para o banco
text:
— Central de atendimento, boa noite. Com quem eu falo?
— É o Ricardo Mendes. Acho que perdi o meu cartão de crédito. Usei o cartão no almoço, e agora não estou achando.
— Entendi, senhor Ricardo. Pode me confirmar a sua data de nascimento?
— Quinze de março de 1985.
— Obrigada. Pronto, o cartão está bloqueado. O novo cartão vai chegar em até sete dias úteis.
— E se alguém usou o cartão hoje?
— Não se preocupe. O senhor pode ver as compras no aplicativo.
translation:
— Customer service, good evening. Who am I speaking to?
— This is Ricardo Mendes. I think I've lost my credit card. I used the card at lunch, and now I can't find it.
— I see, Mr. Ricardo. Can you confirm your date of birth?
— March fifteenth, 1985.
— Thank you. There, the card is blocked. The new card will arrive within seven working days.
— And what if someone used the card today?
— Don't worry. You can see the purchases in the app.

questions.q: Why does Ricardo call?
options: His card didn't work at lunch
He wants to open a new account
He thinks he lost his card
questions.explain: Ricardo says 'Acho que perdi o meu cartão de crédito' (I think I lost my credit card).

questions.q: What does the bank worker ask Ricardo to confirm?
questions.explain: She asks 'Pode me confirmar a sua data de nascimento?', and he gives the date.

questions.q: The bank worker asks 'Com quem eu falo?' What does she want to know?
options: Who he wants to talk to
questions.explain: 'Com quem eu falo?' asks who is on the phone, and Ricardo answers with his name: 'É o Ricardo Mendes'.

topic: online order in the wrong size
title: Pedido 4521
text:
Assunto: Pedido 4521 – tamanho errado
Boa tarde!
No dia 3 de maio, comprei um tênis de corrida, tamanho 39. O pacote chegou ontem, mas, quando abri a caixa, vi que o tênis era 37. Experimentei, e ficou muito apertado.

Eu queria trocar pelo tamanho certo. Preciso devolver o tênis pelo correio? E quem paga o frete? Não quero o dinheiro de volta, só o tênis certo, porque vou correr uma prova de 10 km no dia 1º de junho.

Atenciosamente,
Juliana Castro
translation:
Subject: Order 4521 – wrong size
Good afternoon!
On May 3, I bought a pair of running shoes, size 39. The parcel arrived yesterday, but when I opened the box, I saw that the shoes were a 37. I tried them on, and they were very tight.

I'd like to exchange them for the right size. Do I need to send the shoes back by post? And who pays for the shipping? I don't want my money back, just the right shoes, because I'm going to run a 10 km race on June 1.

Kind regards,
Juliana Castro

questions.q: Why does Juliana write to the shop?
options: To say her parcel has not arrived
To exchange shoes for another size
To order a second pair of running shoes
To get her money back for the shoes
questions.explain: She writes 'Eu queria trocar pelo tamanho certo' (I'd like to exchange them for the right size), and she doesn't want 'o dinheiro de volta'.

questions.q: What size did Juliana order?
questions.explain: She writes 'comprei um tênis de corrida, tamanho 39'.

questions.q: Juliana writes 'ficou muito apertado'. What does she mean?
options: The shoes were the wrong color
questions.explain: She got a 37 instead of a 39, and 'apertado' means tight: the shoes were too small for her.

topic: flat tire on a beach trip
title: Viagem para Ubatuba
text:
Num feriado, Vítor e a namorada, Paula, saíram de São Paulo bem cedo. Eles queriam chegar a Ubatuba antes do almoço. Mas, no meio da serra, ouviram um barulho: o pneu furou!

Os dois não sabiam trocar pneu e ficaram preocupados. Depois de uma hora, um caminhoneiro parou o caminhão e ajudou o casal. Em quinze minutos, o pneu estava trocado.

Eles chegaram a Ubatuba às três da tarde, com muita fome. Na praia, comeram peixe frito e riram muito da aventura.
translation:
On a public holiday, Vítor and his girlfriend, Paula, left São Paulo very early. They wanted to get to Ubatuba before lunch. But in the middle of the mountain road, they heard a noise: they had a flat tire!

Neither of them knew how to change a tire, and they got worried. After an hour, a truck driver stopped his truck and helped the couple. In fifteen minutes, the tire was changed.

They got to Ubatuba at three in the afternoon, very hungry. On the beach, they ate fried fish and laughed a lot about the adventure.

questions.q: What is the story about?
options: A beach trip in heavy rain
A beach trip with no money
A beach trip when they got lost
A beach trip and a flat tire
questions.explain: On the way, 'no meio da serra', they heard a noise: 'o pneu furou!' (they had a flat tire).

questions.q: What time did they arrive in Ubatuba?
questions.explain: The text says 'Eles chegaram a Ubatuba às três da tarde', not before lunch as they wanted.

questions.q: Who was the 'caminhoneiro' who helped them?
questions.explain: He 'parou o caminhão' (stopped his truck): a 'caminhoneiro' drives a 'caminhão'.

topic: diary of a first driving lesson
title: Um dia importante
text:
Terça-feira, 10 de março
Hoje fiz minha primeira aula de direção! Estava nervosa, mas o instrutor, o Sr. Valter, é muito calmo. Primeiro, ele explicou os pedais e os espelhos. Depois, dirigi devagar numa rua tranquila.

Tudo correu bem até a primeira esquina: esqueci de olhar no espelho, e o carro morreu duas vezes! Fiquei com vergonha, mas o Sr. Valter riu e disse que isso acontece com todo mundo.

Na quinta, tenho a segunda aula. Estou com medo, mas também estou animada!
translation:
Tuesday, March 10
Today I had my first driving lesson! I was nervous, but the instructor, Mr. Valter, is very calm. First he explained the pedals and the mirrors. Then I drove slowly along a quiet street.

Everything went well until the first corner: I forgot to look in the mirror, and the car stalled twice! I was embarrassed, but Mr. Valter laughed and said that it happens to everyone.

On Thursday I have my second lesson. I'm scared, but I'm also excited!

questions.q: What is the diary entry about?
options: Her first day as an instructor
questions.explain: She writes 'Hoje fiz minha primeira aula de direção!' (today I had my first driving lesson).

questions.q: What did she forget to do at the corner?
questions.explain: She writes 'esqueci de olhar no espelho' (I forgot to look in the mirror).

questions.q: She writes 'o carro morreu duas vezes'. What happened?
options: The car broke down for good
questions.explain: Here 'morrer' is about the engine: it stopped twice, and Mr. Valter says 'isso acontece com todo mundo' (it happens to everyone).

title: Aulas de forró
text:
Quando era criança, Sofia nunca dançava nas festas. Ela tinha vergonha e achava que não sabia dançar. No ano passado, em Fortaleza, uma colega de trabalho convidou Sofia para uma aula de forró, e ela aceitou.

Nas primeiras aulas, Sofia pisava no pé de todo mundo e errava todos os passos. Mas o professor tinha muita paciência, e os colegas eram simpáticos. Aos poucos, ela aprendeu.

Hoje, Sofia dança forró toda sexta-feira e não tem mais vergonha.
translation:
When she was a child, Sofia never danced at parties. She was shy and thought she couldn't dance. Last year, in Fortaleza, a colleague from work invited Sofia to a forró class, and she accepted.

In the first classes, Sofia stepped on everyone's feet and got all the steps wrong. But the teacher was very patient, and the other students were friendly. Little by little, she learned.

Today Sofia dances forró every Friday and isn't shy anymore.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: Dance helps Sofia stop being shy
Sofia meets her husband at a dance
questions.explain: As a child Sofia 'tinha vergonha' (was shy) and never danced; today she dances forró 'e não tem mais vergonha' (and isn't shy anymore).

questions.q: Who invited Sofia to her first class?
questions.explain: The text says 'uma colega de trabalho convidou Sofia para uma aula de forró'.

questions.q: 'Aos poucos, ela aprendeu.' How did Sofia learn?
questions.explain: 'Aos poucos' means little by little: at first she 'errava todos os passos' (got every step wrong), and then she slowly got better.

title: O meu bairro
text:
Moro no mesmo bairro de Salvador desde criança, mas ele mudou muito. Quando eu era pequeno, as ruas eram calmas, e as crianças jogavam bola na frente das casas. À tarde, a minha avó conversava com as vizinhas na calçada.

Hoje, há mais prédios, carros e barulho. A antiga mercearia virou uma farmácia, e o campo de futebol virou um supermercado.

Mas algumas coisas continuam iguais: a padaria da esquina ainda vende o melhor pão da cidade, e os vizinhos ainda se cumprimentam.
translation:
I've lived in the same neighborhood in Salvador since I was a child, but it has changed a lot. When I was little, the streets were quiet, and children played ball in front of the houses. In the afternoons, my grandmother chatted with the neighbors on the sidewalk.

Today there are more buildings, cars and noise. The old grocery store has become a pharmacy, and the football field has become a supermarket.

But some things are still the same: the bakery on the corner still sells the best bread in the city, and the neighbors still greet each other.

questions.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: Why he wants to leave his neighborhood
How he moved to a new neighborhood
Why his neighborhood is the best in Salvador
questions.explain: He has lived there 'desde criança', and 'ele mudou muito' (it has changed a lot): today there are more buildings, cars and noise.

questions.q: What did the writer's grandmother do in the afternoons?
options: She played ball with the children
She baked bread for the bakery
She sold fruit at the market
questions.explain: The text says 'À tarde, a minha avó conversava com as vizinhas na calçada' (on the sidewalk).

questions.q: 'A antiga mercearia virou uma farmácia.' What does this mean?
options: The old shop is now a pharmacy
The old shop is next to a pharmacy
The old shop moved to another street
The pharmacy closed down years ago
questions.explain: 'Virar' here means to become: where the old 'mercearia' (grocery store) was, there is now a pharmacy.
